````` ::: ::: **Expected:** 1,156 rows and 38 variables. The performance fields are `MP` (minutes played) and `PTS` (points). The season counts include `season_1` with 82 rows but only 71 complete game records, because some rows have no box-score values; that is why LM3 filters for non-missing performance values. # 3 · T — Transformation (27 min) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM3: first five seasons with complete game records kobe_df <- nba_df |> filter(Season %in% paste0("season_", 1:5), !is.na(MP), !is.na(PTS)) nrow(kobe_df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 334 ``` ::: ::: **Expected:** 334 complete game rows. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM4: select what matters and create the rate kobe_df <- kobe_df |> select(Season, MP, PTS) |> mutate(season_number = readr::parse_number(Season), ppm = PTS / MP) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM5: summarize and arrange by season_number kobe_table_df <- kobe_df |> group_by(Season, season_number) |> summarize(games = n(), points = sum(PTS), minutes = sum(MP), ppm = points / minutes, .groups = "drop") |> arrange(season_number) |> mutate(ppm = round(ppm, 3)) kobe_table_df ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
````` ::: ::: **Expected table:** | Season | games | points | minutes | ppm | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | season_1 | 71 | 539 | 1087.70 | 0.496 | | season_2 | 79 | 1220 | 2042.93 | 0.597 | | season_3 | 50 | 996 | 1882.57 | 0.529 | | season_4 | 66 | 1485 | 2509.82 | 0.592 | | season_5 | 68 | 1938 | 2778.23 | 0.697 | # 4 · V — Visualization (20 min) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # LM6: time-ordered point plot ggplot(kobe_table_df, aes(x = season_number, y = ppm)) + geom_point(size = 3, color = "#12263A") + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:5) + labs(x = "Season number", y = "Points per minute", title = "Kobe's scoring rate climbed across his first five seasons") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](etv02_nba_solution_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: *(Optional companion plot — the measurement beat made visible:)* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(kobe_table_df, aes(x = season_number, y = points)) + geom_point(size = 3, color = "#A63D2F") + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:5) + labs(x = "Season number", y = "Total points", title = "Raw totals dip in season 3, the 50-game lockout season") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](etv02_nba_solution_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: **Teaching note:** the two plots disagree about season 3. Totals decline because the season had only 50 games; the rate remains near the surrounding seasons. That disagreement is the measurement lesson. # 5 · Interpretation & final answer (10 min) **Model answer:** *"Kobe's scoring rate rose from about 0.496 points per minute in season 1 to about 0.697 in season 5, an increase of roughly 41%. The climb was not perfectly steady: season 3 has fewer total points because the lockout limited the schedule to 50 games, while its per-minute rate remained near 0.53. A raw total would have misled us there."* Required elements: **direction, magnitude, and the lockout caveat** — direction/size/caveat is the CLO 4.5 trio for this cycle.
